_comment: Per-PREDICTIONS-bank ledger, read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/carryforward_check.py (round 369). CLAUDE.md rule D-013 has two halves -- bank predictions BEFORE measuring, then score them honestly -- and nothing in this program ever checked the second half. Five banks had been silently dropped (23, 132, 362, 368, and this round's own 369 until it is scored). An entry is `scored` (naming the round that discharged it, the file, and a sentence that must still be findable there -- K002 re-reads it, it is not trusted) or `unscored` (naming an `owner` track and a `why`). A `remainder` field records predictions a discharge left out; it raises a K004 WARNING, never an error, so a partial discharge stays visible without the check crying wolf. DISCOVERY IS A REPO-WIDE FILENAME SWEEP, not this file: a bank on disk with no entry here is a K001 ERROR, so adding a bank under a seventh naming convention cannot silently escape. The scanner behind `--suggest` is a bootstrap and a rot detector, never the authority -- its first version got 5 of 13 verdicts wrong in both directions, which is why this file exists. ROUND 375: a `scored` entry's `remainder` field means OUTSTANDING PREDICTIONS -- the ones the discharge did not reach -- and carryforward_check's K004 warns on its PRESENCE. Prose that is NOT a debt belongs in `note`, added round 375. Rounds 373 and 374 had written narrative into `remainder` (both texts open 'None outstanding'), so the check reported two partial discharges the record itself denies; their text moved to `note` unchanged. `note` is a DECLARATION and nothing re-derives it: see carryforward_check.py's docstring for why a scanner that decides whether a `remainder` really means debt would re-introduce the 5-of-13 prose classifier round 369 replaced with this ledger.
_bootstrap: Bootstrapped by round 369 from a prose scan of state/research-state.md, state/research-state-archive.md and knowledge/*.md, then HAND-ADJUDICATED bank by bank against the corpus. Eleven entries (15, 17, 24, 27, 29, 31, 105, 112, 137, 366, 367) had their quote or attribution corrected by hand -- the scanner had credited round 137 with round 353's P1 about round 137's TREE, credited round 105 with a sentence about round 27, and missed round 366's lowercase "P4/P5/P6 hit" entirely. Two banks carry no round number in their path at all (nuc/predictions-e1.md, nuc/predictions-e2.md, mission-scoped rather than round-scoped); the checker reports them as unnumbered and does not require entries for them.
